::: {#hero-heading}

I am a PhD candidate in Sociology at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. My research examines how the content of work changes and how skills, tasks, and other work requirements spread, accumulate, and recede across occupations, jobs, and organizations amid rapid technological change, including advances in artificial intelligence. Using network analysis, formal models, computational experiments, and longitudinal data, I study why these changes follow unequal paths through the occupational structure and how they contribute to labor-market polarization and inequality. In a parallel line of research, I study relational persistence: when available alternatives threaten an existing tie, how opportunity sets shape tie stability, and who forms the replacement tie after a relationship dissolves. Emerging work extends this relational perspective to urban and intergenerational mobility.
